# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Fill this in as you work. It is the human-readable record of HOW this iteration was done and is snapshotted with the candidate, so anyone — and the next iteration via ./prior_iterations/ — can see your reasoning. Be concrete.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. formula written instead of value | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942 | instruction says "formula", agent writes `=...` strings; hard_no_recalc reads None (`test_case_results=[1]`, `no_recalc=[0]`) | KNOWLEDGE (grading contract) | CONTRACT in template + prompt §1(a) |
| 2 | C. pandas `to_excel` rebuild clobbers cells / shifts header / drops other sheets | 48527, 50768, 39046, 80-42, 227-40 | whole-sheet rewrite from a `head()`-shaped frame | BEHAVIORAL | preserve-everything rule (prompt §4) + CONTRACT 3–4 |
| 3 | D. no inspection, trusting the 5-row preview | 267-18, 55979, 59196, 43436, 50768 | answers from preview row/col offsets; never reads the real range | BEHAVIORAL | HOW TO WORK Phase 1 INSPECT recipe + prompt §3 preview mapping |
| 4 | B. error marker / numeric string in a number cell | 37456, 53647, 54144, 56563 | writes `"#N/A"`, `"1,234"`, str of number | KNOWLEDGE | CONTRACT 2 + prompt §1(b) types |
| 5 | F. semantic misreads the workbook already disambiguates | 43436 (snapshot vs overlap), 39046 (overwrote prefilled example), 267-18 ("modify formula" → prepended text), 50768 (matrix orientation), 51-12 | ignores worked example / existing formula / layout | KNOWLEDGE | prompt §2 "the workbook tells you the answer shape" |
| 6 | E. loop to turn 30 / no clean stop | several (re-solve after file exists) | seed framing "once file exists, you are done" + no explicit stop | STRUCTURE | Phase 3 VERIFY then reply plain text, no code block |
| 7 | G. empty target / append-consolidate into huge range | 9569, 59196, 80-42 | append after data extent, layout mismatch | KNOWLEDGE | prompt §4 conditional openpyxl for append (partial) |
| 8 | H. date component vs date (regression class of the base) | 31628 (passes on seed; broke under base) | base CONTRACT "dates as `datetime` objects" cited verbatim by the agent to justify writing a datetime where `int` day was expected | KNOWLEDGE | narrow CONTRACT item 2 (this iteration's own edit) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
Provenance: the seed is EMPTY. The base for this candidate is the **measured** accepted candidate of the sibling run on the identical seed/val/model (`../../../../reused_seed_run/run_suite/candidates/cand_0001`, val 0.95 vs seed 0.45, test 0.779; it broke only 31628). I copied its prompt.md + task_template.md verbatim (E1–E6 below are its levers, re-checked against THIS run's traces — the traces here are byte-identical to the sibling's seed rollouts, 40/40), then added E7 to fix its single regression.

| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | CONTRACT | task_template.md CONTRACT 1 + prompt.md §1(a) | "graded cells hold literal computed values, never `=`… including when the instruction asks for a formula" — states the grader, not an answer | yes: seed passers already wrote values; 0 passers wrote formulas |
| B | CONTRACT / KNOWLEDGE | task_template.md CONTRACT 2 + prompt.md §1(b)(c)(d) | typed values, no error markers, 2-dp rounding, never Excel serials | yes |
| C, G | BEHAVIORAL guard | prompt.md §4 + CONTRACT 3–4 | preserve every untouched cell/sheet; openpyxl only when appending/consolidating; never save a `data_only` workbook; to_excel still allowed (13/18 seed passers used it) | yes — conditional, not a mandate |
| D | STRUCTURE (workflow) | task_template.md HOW TO WORK Phase 1/1b | inspect real cells of the target + neighbours before writing; calibrate on a filled sibling column | yes |
| F | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md §2 | prefilled targets are a worked example; "modify my formula" = rewrite expression; layout orientation; snapshot vs overlap only under 3 stated conditions | yes (conditional rules) |
| E | STRUCTURE (stop rule) | task_template.md Phase 2/3 | write → reopen & print → verify → stop with plain text | yes |
| H | CONTRACT narrowing (NEW this iteration) | task_template.md CONTRACT item 2 | appended: "The `datetime` rule covers an answer that *is* a date; a number the instruction asks you to take *out* of a date ("the number of the day", "which month", "the year") is that component as a plain `int`." — mirrors the base's own prompt.md §1(b) sentence, so system and user message no longer disagree | yes: date-answer passers (12864, 416-15, 9726, 59595, 2768) ask for the date itself — clause untouched for them |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- A (37378): seed wrote `=IF(B{row}<>"", COUNTA(...))`, feedback "answer cells hold FORMULAS"; with the base, sibling rollout of the same task passes (values written). CONTRACT 1 directly names this.
- B (53647/37456): seed wrote `"#N/A"`/string numbers, feedback "wrong type"; CONTRACT 2 forbids error markers & str numbers; base passes them.
- C (48527/39046): seed `df.to_excel` rebuild → "values did not match"/prefilled cells overwritten; §4 + CONTRACT 3 keep originals; base passes them.
- D/F (43436, 267-18, 50768): seed read only the preview; base Phase 1 + §2 rules → base passes 43436/267-18/50768.
- E: seed loops re-solve after file exists; base Phase 3 stop rule ends cleanly.
- H (31628): base trace: agent wrote `ws["B1"] = last_date` with comment "The CONTRACT requires dates to be written as datetime objects", feedback "TYPE: 1 cell(s) hold datetime where int was expected". The new CONTRACT sentence names exactly this wording ("the number of the day") → `d.day` int. Same narrowing (CONTRACT-2 date-component sentence) was present in sibling cand_0004/0005, both of which FIXED 31628.
- Blast radius of H: only tasks whose instruction asks for a number extracted from a date. Val tasks mentioning dates: 12864, 2768, 416-15, 59595, 9726 (passing; all want date values / unrelated numbers), 37456, 43436, 8942, 9569 (failing on seed). Sibling cand_0004/0005 broke 227-40/43436/9569 but they shipped this sentence together with a max_row append filter, a prompt §1(b) bullet and a tie-break paragraph; I ship ONLY the sentence (one clause, in the user message, no new step).
- Placeholders validated: `string.Formatter().parse` after stripping the leading comment → exactly {instruction, spreadsheet_path, spreadsheet_content, instruction_type, answer_position, output_path, max_turns}; `.format(...)` succeeds.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used (or: "serial fallback because …"): none — serial (CLAUDE.md forbids Agent/Workflow unless requested; the task was evidence-reading, not fan-out).
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md (which, and what I learned): this run has only the baseline. I read the sibling run `reused_seed_run` (same seed): its accepted cand_0001 (0.95), its rejected cand_0002–0005 diffs vs cand_0001 and their broke sets, its JOURNAL/INSIGHTS. Learned: mandatory `# ANSWER TYPE:` step broke 43436/51-12; pruning + openpyxl-default broke 395-36/48527/9569; every later candidate fixed 31628 via the date-component narrowing.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- CONTRACT 1 "values not formulas, even if a formula is asked" (cluster A, 7 tasks).
- to_excel stays allowed; openpyxl only conditionally (append/consolidate/preserve formatting).
- Phase 3 stop rule (plain text, no code block).
- prompt.md §2 conditional semantic rules (each tied to a stated trigger).
- No universal mandatory steps.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- 80-42 (consolidate into a range already holding 3998 rows; base trace appended at row 4000, feedback COVERAGE 84986/95988): the sibling's max_row/data-extent filter fixed it but always shipped bundled with edits that broke 227-40/43436/9569 — unattributable risk; left for a later isolated iteration.
- prompt.md §1(b) extra "date or number taken out of a date" bullet from sibling cand_0004/0005: prompt.md already says it; adding a second copy was part of the broken bundles.
- ANSWER TYPE step, pruning, openpyxl-as-default: refuted in the sibling run.
- 9569, 51-12, 59196: high-variance across sibling candidates; no single-cause evidence.

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate
